goal: After this you can read, print and calculate with struct members, compare two structs member by member, use a struct inside a struct, and put an array inside a struct.
warmup: A shopkeeper has a bill with item name, price and quantity. To find the total he multiplies the price and quantity on the bill. To check whether two bills are the same, he compares item, price and quantity one by one, not by staring at the whole paper. Struct members work the same way: each member is used like a normal variable.
definition: Every data member of a struct behaves like an ordinary variable of its own type. A double member can be used in arithmetic, an int member in a comparison, a string member with cin. The only things you cannot do directly with a whole struct variable are cin >> s, cout << s and s1 == s2. Work member by member. One thing you can do with a whole struct is assign it: s2 = s1. A struct can also contain another struct (nested structure) or an array.
howItWorks: Reading and printing: cin >> s1.id; and cout << s1.name; Each member is treated alone. Arithmetic: s1.price * s1.qty, or s1.qty = s1.qty + 2; the member is just a variable with a dotted name. Comparing two structs: s1 == s2 gives a compile error, because C++ does not know what 'equal' should mean for your type. Compare the members you care about, joined with &&: s1.id == s2.id && s1.name == s2.name. Nested structures: if a Student has a member birth of type Date, you reach the year with TWO dots: s1.birth.year. Read the dots left to right: s1, then its birth, then its year. Arrays inside structs: a struct can hold an array, for example int marks[3];. You reach one mark as r.marks[i], and you can loop over it as usual. Putting it together: the exam program reads a name and three marks into one struct, computes the average and the grade, and stores them back into the same struct. Everything about one student stays inside one variable, and no function is needed. The first trace shows the copy r2 = r1. The second shows a nested struct comparison. The third shows an array member inside a loop.

worked.problem: Declare a struct Rectangle (length, width). Read the length and width of rectangle 1, make rectangle 2 a copy with the length doubled, then print both areas and say which rectangle is bigger.
pseudocode: IF a1 > a2 PRINT Rectangle 1 ELSE PRINT Rectangle 2
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[/Read r1.length and r1.width/]
  B --> C[r2 = r1]
  C --> D[r2.length = r2.length * 2]
  D --> E[Compute a1 and a2]
  E --> F[/Print a1 and a2/]
  F --> G{a1 > a2?}
  G -- Yes --> H[/Print Rectangle 1 is bigger/]
  G -- No --> I[/Print Rectangle 2 is bigger/]
  H --> J([End])
  I --> J

worked.problem: Write a program with a struct Result holding a name, three marks, an average and a grade. Read a name and three marks, compute the average, assign the grade (A for 85 or more, B for 70 or more, C for 50 or more, otherwise F) and print the result.
pseudocode: FOR i = 0 to 2: READ r.marks[i], total = total + r.marks[i]
IF average >= 85 grade A ELSE IF >= 70 grade B ELSE IF >= 50 grade C ELSE grade F
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[/Read r.name/]
  B --> C[total = 0, i = 0]
  C --> D{i < 3?}
  D -- Yes --> E[/Read r.marks i/]
  E --> F[total = total + r.marks i]
  F --> G[i = i + 1]
  G --> D
  D -- No --> H[r.average = total / 3.0]
  H --> I[Set r.grade by average]
  I --> J[/Print name, average, grade/]
  J --> K([End])

variations.when: Input goes straight into the member.
Output uses one member at a time.
Members are ordinary numbers in an expression.
Checking two records. There is no == for whole structs.
A member is itself a struct. Use a dot for each level.
A fixed set of values inside a record. Dot, then index.

mistakes.error: g++ reports: no match for 'operator==' (operand types are 'Student' and 'Student'). Compare the members.

mistakes.wrong:
Student a;
cin >> a;   // read the whole struct
mistakes.error: g++ reports: no match for 'operator>>' (operand types are 'std::istream' and 'Student'). Read member by member.

mistakes.wrong:
Student a;
a.day = 5;   // day is inside birth
mistakes.error: g++ reports: 'struct Student' has no member named 'day' (the same message pattern for any missing member). Use one dot per level of nesting.

examTips: Whole struct: assignment (s2 = s1) is allowed. cin, cout and == on a whole struct are NOT allowed.
To compare two records, join member comparisons with &&.
Nested structures need one dot per level: student.birth.year.
An array member is read like record.marks[i]. Remember the loop variable.
Use 3.0 (not 3) when you divide a total by a count to keep the decimals.
romanSummary: Struct ka har member apne type ke normal variable ki tarah kaam karta hai: cin, cout, calculation aur comparison sab member par hote hain.
s2 = s1; poora struct copy kar deta hai, lekin cin >> s1, cout << s1 aur s1 == s2 direct nahi chalte.
Do structs ko compare karna ho to har member ko alag compare karo aur && se jodo.
Nested struct mein har level ke liye ek dot lagta hai: s1.birth.year.
Struct ke andar array bhi ho sakta hai: r.marks[i].

practice.prompt: Which is NOT allowed for two variables a and b of the same struct type?
practice.hint: One of them has no meaning for a whole struct.
practice.explanation: C++ has no built-in == for structs. Compare member by member. Assignment a = b is fine.

practice.explanation: Go from the outer struct to the inner one with dots.

practice.hint: a is not changed by edits to b.

practice.explanation: The year goes from 2004 to 2005, the day and month stay 14 and 8.

practice.hint: Structs cannot be compared with == directly.
practice.explanation: Compare the members one by one and join them with &&.

practice.hint: Struct name, dot, array name, index.
practice.explanation: An array member is reached with the dot, then the index.

practice.prompt: Struct Student has int marks[3] and double average. Write the statement that stores the average of the three marks in s.average.
practice.explanation: Using 3.0 avoids integer division, so the decimals are kept.

quiz.prompt: Which of these works for struct variables?

options: A struct that has another struct as a member
Two structs with the same name
A struct declared inside main only
quiz.answer: A struct that has another struct as a member
quiz.explanation: For example a Student with a Date member.

quiz.prompt: To check that two Student records are equal you should
options: compare every member and join the tests with &&
quiz.answer: compare every member and join the tests with &&
quiz.explanation: You must define what equal means by testing each member.
